title: Designing intentional experiences: build for the person on the other side, not the persona
summary: Cris Pop explains how Thunder Talks events start from an imagined newcomer's feelings rather than logistics or content. He extends the same empathy to feedback and to product or community decisions, asking what the other person actually needs and designing for people instead of personas.

principles.text: Start event design by sitting in the attendee's empty chair, not with logistics or content.
principles.quote: When we organize events, we don't begin with logistics or content. Instead, we sit in an empty chair and imagine: I've never been here before. I'm not sure if I belong. How do I want to be welcomed?

principles.text: Ask what people actually need, not whether they'll like what you built.
principles.quote: Instead of limiting to questions like "Will they like what we've built?", you go deeper and shape what do they actually need. This way, people feel understood before they even realize they needed to be.

principles.text: Design for the quiet introvert in the back row to make participation feel safe.
principles.quote: All of this started by imagining the introvert in the back row, the one who carries a question they won’t ask out loud.

principles.text: Welcome people as friends into your home, with small personal gestures like a book and a message.
principles.quote: We welcome people not as guests, but as friends stepping into our home. We meet them, we try to know them, we do our best to make them feel comfortable.

principles.text: Honest feedback must be effective: shape it so the truth can be received, not just heard.
principles.quote: We don’t have to dilute the truth. We just need to make space for it to land, human to human.

principles.text: Put yourself in the community member's, customer's or attendee's seat to strip away assumptions.
principles.quote: Because when you start from yourself, from your humanness, you begin to strip away assumptions. You stop designing for personas and start designing for people.
